title: Techniques for the Evolution of Robust Pentose-fermenting Yeast for Bioconversion of Lignocellulose to Ethanol
protocol: Prepare hydrolyzates using 18 to 20% initial biomass dry weight in the pretreatment reaction.
Use AFEX CSH, PSGHL, and SGH with nitrogen supplements N1 or N2 as specified for evolution, isolation, and ranking procedures.
Fortify SGH to a 42:1 molar carbon to nitrogen ratio (C:N) for SGH-N1 using urea and specific amino acids and vitamins.
Designate SGH fortified to a 37:1 C:N with urea and soy flour as SGH-N2, providing ~12% of N from primary amino nitrogen (PAN) and 88% as urea.
Acquire a lyophilized culture of the parent strain Scheffersomyces stipitis NRRL Y-7124 (CBS 7573).
Prepare glycerol stock cultures as directed for maintenance at -80 °C.
Streak glycerol stocks to yeast malt peptone dextrose (YM) agar plates.
Incubate plates at 25 °C for 48-72 hours.
Store developed plates up to a week at 4 °C.
Prepare Optimal Defined Medium (ODM).
Use ODM in all precultures and cultures for fermentation performance bioassays.
Use ODM for ethanol challenged, xylose-fed continuous culture evolution.
Analyze cell biomass using a cuvette- or micro-plate reading spectrophotometer.
Measure culture absorbance at 620 nm (A620).

Quantitate sugars, ethanol, furfural, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), and acetic acid in culture samples using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) or robotic enzymatic determination of glucose and xylose.
Inoculate a preculture of strain NRRL Y-7124 by transferring cells from YM agar to 75 ml ODM + 150 g/L xylose.
Incubate the precultures in 125 ml flasks closed with silicon sponge plugs for 24 hours at 25 °C with shaking (150 rpm, 1" orbit).
Thaw frozen aliquots of 6-12% glucan AFEX CSH in cold water.
Adjust pH to 5 if needed and filter sterilize prior to preparing a dilution series in 96-well microplates.
Fill the microplates with 50 μl per well and inoculate each well with a few microliters of preculture to achieve an initial absorbance (620 nm) A620 ≥0.1.
Incubate the plates statically for 24-48 hours at 25 °C in a plastic box with a wet paper towel for humidity.
Transfer 1-5 μl from the most concentrated hydrolyzate dilution that visibly grew to A620 >1, to each well of a new hydrolyzate dilution series to achieve an initial A620 ≥0.1.
Monitor growth culture A620 in microplates with a spectrophotometer.
Use an uninoculated dilution series as a control and blank.
Plate lids are left on during monitoring to prevent contamination, and the readings adjusted accordingly.
Pool four wells (200 μl) of the greatest hydrolyzate concentration colonized.
Mix pooled cultures 1:1 with 20% sterile glycerol in cryovials.
Freeze cells in 10% glycerol at -80°C.
Repeat steps until growth in 12% glucan AFEX CSH is consistently visible at 24 hours.
Streak selected glycerol stocks of adaptation cultures to YM agar.
Inoculate 50 μl of 3% or 6% glucan AFEX CSH (pH 5) in each of three microplate wells with streaks from the plate.
Incubate microplates for 24 hours as previously described.
Pool replicate colonized wells at the highest hydrolyzate strength showing strong growth.
Dilution plate to YM or 6% glucan AFEX CSH agar.
Prepare 6% glucan AFEX CSH agar as a 1:1 mix of filter sterilized 12% glucan AFEX CSH with warm autoclaved 30 g/L agar solution.
Pick 5 single colonies from the highest dilution plate showing growth after 24-48 hours incubation at 25°C to freeze as glycerol stock cultures.
Streak each colony to a YM plate.
Incubate plates for 24 hours.
Transfer a developed streak of cells with a sterile loop to a small volume of 10% glycerol, mix to suspend cells.
Distribute the suspension to 2-3 cryovials and freeze at -80°C.
Transfer cells from 48 hr plates streaked from glycerol stocks to pH 7 potassium phosphate buffer (0.4 mM) to prepare cell suspensions with A620 = 10.
Use 1 µl of each suspension to inoculate each of four wells of 50 µl 3% glucan hydrolyzate to initial A620 = 0.2.
Incubate microplates 24 hr as in step 2.3.
Prepare the 3% glucan AFEX CSH at pH 5 by diluting 12% glucan AFEX CSH 1:3 with sterile water.
Transfer two 24 hr microplate wells to inoculate 25 ml precultures of pH 5 12% glucan AFEX CSH used at 50% of full strength.
Incubate precultures in 50 ml flasks with silicon sponge closures for 24 hr at 25 °C, ~150 rpm (1" orbit).
Prepare the half-strength 12% glucan AFEX CSH by diluting the hydrolyzate 1:1 with sterile water.
Use half-strength hydrolyzate precultures to inoculate similar 25 ml growth cultures to initial A620 = 0.1.
Incubate the growth cultures as above and sample daily (0.2 ml).
Monitor accumulations of biomass (A620) and concentrations of sugars and fermentation products (HPLC).
Inoculate precultures of 75 ml ODM with 150 g/L xylose in 125 ml flasks by loop transfer from YM glycerol streaks.
Incubate precultures for 24 hours at 25 °C, 150 rpm.
Inoculate similar 75 ml test cultures containing ODM with 75 g/L glucose and 75 g/L xylose at pH 6.5 using the precultures.
Shake flasks at 25 °C, 150 rpm.
Sample daily.
Prepare continuous culture feed medium ODM with 60-100 g/L xylose and 20-50 g/L ethanol at pH 6.3 ± 0.2.
Transfer a representative AFEX CSH-tolerant colony from a 48 hr YM plate to 75 ml of ethanol-free ODM (100 g/L xylose) in 125 ml flasks for continuous culture inoculum preparation.
Incubate inoculum at 25 °C, 150 rpm for 24 hours.
Inoculate a continuous culture holding volume of ODM at pH 6.3 ± 0.2 containing 100 g/L xylose and 20 g/L ethanol with ~5-10 ml of a preculture concentrate of an AFEX CSH-tolerant isolate.
Maintain the culture in a jacketed 100 ml spinner flask at 25 °C, stirred at 200 rpm, equipped with a pH electrode and temperature-controlled circulating water bath.
Set up the feed medium to dose using a pH-actuated pump when the culture pH drops to 5.4.
Feed the culture with ODM containing 100 g/L xylose and 50 g/L ethanol to stop further pH drop.
Maintain the volume at 100 ml continuously skimming the culture surface with an effluent pump.
Measure effluent and draw samples (1-2 ml) from continuous cultures every 48-72 hours for analysis.
Make serial 1:10 dilutions of samples in buffer and spread plate the dilutions to YM agar to find viable cell concentration.
Calculate the dilution rate (D) based on effluent collection rates (Q), with D = Q/VR.
Isolate glycerol stocks regularly from viability plates containing buffered sample dilutions forming 30-100 colonies.
Flood isolated plates with ~5 ml of 10% glycerol for cryovial preparation.
Maintain cultures by stopping continuous culture and restarting using the most current glycerol stock(s).
Streak glycerol stocks onto YM agar to transfer 24-48 hr cells to a pre-culture of ethanol-free ODM.
Inoculate 100 ml holding volume of ODM with concentrate of precultured yeast to initial A620 0.5.
Allow the culture to grow batch-wise to stationary phase before restarting feed medium flow.
Start continuous culture feed at a low dilution rate (~0.01 hr-1) using ODM + 60 g/L xylose + ethanol ranging from 30 to 50 g/L.
Gradually increase ethanol concentration in the feed toward 50 g/L over time.
Capture advanced populations in glycerol stocks regularly.
Optionally, apply ultra-violet (UV) irradiation monthly to glycerol stock populations for reinoculating continuous cultures.
Resuspend colonies from glycerol stock streaks in 10 ml of ODM containing 60 g/L xylose.
Pool all stocks in a single sterile flask.
Apply the pooled cell suspension at ~5 x 10^8 viable cells/ml to cover the bottoms of 4-5 Petri plates with 6 ml/plate.
Expose each open culture plate to UV light from the source for 45 min at around 56 cm distance in a biological safety cabinet.
Dilute plate cell suspensions before and after irradiation.
Estimate kill rate based on colony forming units.
Transfer the UV-exposed cultures (24-30 ml) to a foil-covered 50 ml flask.
Incubate at 25 °C and 150 rpm for 24 hr to allow repopulation to ~1 x 10^8 viable S. stipitis cells/ml.
Use the repopulated mutagenized culture to inoculate continuous cultures to ~1 x 10^7 viable cells/ml.
Restart the ethanol-enriched ODM + 60 g/L xylose medium feed to continue the selection process.
Streak selected glycerol stock cultures to YM agar.
Transfer each evolved population from streaks to 75 ml precultures in ODM with 150 g/L glucose.
Incubate the precultures for 96 hours at 25 °C, 150 rpm (1" orbit) in 125 ml flasks.
Harvest each culture and suspend cells to 30 ml with an initial A620 of 40 in ODM +60 g/L xylose + 30-45 g/L ethanol.
Incubate the suspended cultures at 25 °C, 150 rpm (1" orbit) in 50 ml flasks with silicon sponge closures.
Draw samples twice daily for monitoring xylose uptake by HPLC analysis.
Prepare precultures of each evolved population by loop transfer to 75 ml ODM with 150 g/L xylose in 125 ml flasks.
Incubate the prepared cultures for 96 hours at 25 °C, 150 rpm (1" orbit).
Inoculate test cultures to a low initial A620 of 0.1 in 25 ml ODM + 60 g/L xylose + 30-45 g/L ethanol in 125 ml flasks.
Incubate the test cultures at 25 °C, 300 rpm (1" orbit) and sample periodically for analysis.
Select glycerol stock populations showing superior ability to grow on and ferment xylose in the presence of ethanol.
Streak plates using selected glycerol stock populations.
Prepare dense, buffered cell suspensions with an A620 of 5 from streak plates.
Inoculate precultures in 96-deep well plates to achieve an A620 of 0.5 using prepared cell suspensions.
Incubate precultures in 96-well deep well plates mixed 1:1 with PSGHL and ODM + 50 g/L xylose without ethanol at 25 °C, 400 rpm, 1" orbit for 48 hr.
Inoculate sixteen 1 ml replicate cultures to initial A620 ~0.5 in 1:1 PSGHL:ODM+50 g/L xylose with 20, 30, or 40 g/L ethanol for each different glycerol stock population.
Incubate enrichment cultures similarly to precultures.
Harvest the culture wells with the highest ethanol concentration allowing growth and xylose use.
Plate each cell line on YM agar to obtain prevalent single colonies.
Preserve obtained single colonies in glycerol.
Pick ten colonies per cell line.
Streak each picked colony to a YM agar plate for glycerol stock preparation.
Inoculate pre-cultures of NRRL Y-7124 (parent), AFEX CSH-tolerant evolved isolate, and continuous culture evolved population with enhanced ability to use xylose in the presence of ethanol.
Dilute PSGHL with water to provide a series of increasing concentrations.
Prepare a 96-well microplate for each of the three cell lines by using each PSGHL dilution to fill 8 wells with 50 µl.
Inoculate each 50 µl micro-culture of the dilution series to an initial A620 ~0.1-0.5.

Continue the evolution of yeast in increasing strengths of PSGHL until cultures are able to grow in full strength hydrolyzate at a stable 14-d average ratio of ΔA620 per Δtime for serial transfers over four months.
Obtain single-cell isolates directly from full strength PSGHL final adaptation plates by dilution plating to YM agar.
Pick ten large colonies for each of the three cell lines and bar streak to YM plates to prepare glycerol stocks.
Inoculate a preculture for each cell line by loop from glycerol stock streaks.
Incubate the inoculated cultures 24 hours on 30 ml ODM + 50 g/L xylose in 50 ml flasks at 25 °C and 150 rpm.
Inoculate microplate wells with 50 µl of 50% PSGHL from precultures to an initial A620 ~0.2.
Incubate the inoculated plates statically for 48 hours.
Spread 0.1 ml of each enriched culture onto PSGHL gradient agar plates ranging from 0 to 50% strength hydrolyzate, delivering approximately 300-400 viable cells per plate.
Pick 10 single colonies per cell line from the highest possible hydrolyzate concentration area of the gradient.
Streak picked colonies on YM for glycerol stock preparation.
Inoculate wells of 96-well microplates to initial A620 ~0.2 with a range of hydrolyzate concentrations from 50 to 100% and ethanol from 10 to 40 g/L as an alternative approach.
Incubate the inoculated plates for 72-96 hours under appropriate conditions.
Isolate ten single colonies from wells showing growth in the harshest hydrolyzate-ethanol combinations via dilution plating.
Prepare glycerol stocks of isolated colonies.
Pick a bead of cells from glycerol streaks prepared from 30 isolates.
Duplicate picked cells into wells containing ODM + 50 g/L xylose and incubate for 48 hours.
Prepare 50% PSGHL by mixing PSGHL with ODM + 10 g/L glucose + 50 g/L xylose in a 1:1 ratio.
Transfer 50 μl of ODM pre-cultures to each of two 50% PSGHL challenge culture wells for isolates and controls.
Incubate the challenge cultures for 72 hours.
Use two test media for screening isolates: 60% PSGHL + ODM nutrients and 75% PSGHL + ODM + YM nutrients.
Add ODM nutrients (excluding sugars) at half of the standard strength as used with 50 g/L sugar to both test media.
As designated, add YM nutrients (excluding sugars) at half of the standard strength of 3 g/L yeast extract, 3 g/L malt extract, and 5 g/L peptone for the second test medium.
Inoculate test cultures by transferring 50 μl of 72 hr 50% PSGHL challenge pre-cultures to inoculate 1,000 μl in initial A620 ~0.5 for five deep wells for each test media.
Pipette the contents of a well daily into a microfuge tube and centrifuge at 5,533 x g for 15 min to obtain supernate for ethanol, glucose, and xylose high throughput analyses.
Measure biomass as A620 in 96-well micro-plates with 200 μl/well using a spectrophotometer.
Calculate dimensionless relative performance indices (RPI) for ranking isolates in each of the five experiments.

Determine the statistical parameter F using the formula F = (X-Xavg)/s, where X is the performance parameter, Xavg is the average, and s is the standard deviation of X observed across all isolates within a given experiment.
Calculate relative performance based on rate (RPIR) with the formula RPIR = (2+FR) × 100/4.
Calculate relative performance based on yield (RPIY) using the formula RPIY = (2+FY) × 100/4.
Calculate the average of RPI values for each isolate within a given hydrolyzate experiment as RPIavg = (RPIY +RPIR)/2, giving equal weighting to yield and rate contributions.
Compute RPIoverall across the n types of hydrolyzates tested.
Sum [(RPIY + RPIR)/2]i for i = 1 to n.
Divide the sum by n to get RPIoverall.
Rank each isolate in an experimental set of 30 isolates and 2 controls based on RPIoverall.
Select the top percentage of isolates from primary screening for secondary screen.
Choose the top 20% of strains from the initial 150 tested for further evaluation.
Compare the top performers from the primary screen on multiple complete hydrolyzates in the secondary screen.
Compare top PSGHL performers on 6% glucan AFEX CSH and SGH amended with two levels of nitrogen, SGH-N1 and SGH-N2.
Screen the 30 isolates that were the top performers in the primary deep well plate screen of PSGHL.
Begin cultivations by picking a bead of cells from glycerol streaks to duplicate deep wells of 1 ml ODM + 50 g/L xylose as before.
Incubate the duplicated deep wells for 48 hours in the deep well plate system.
Transfer 50 µl of ODM precultures to 50% SGH challenge cultures.
Prepare 50% SGH by mixing SGH 1:1 with sugarless ODM + 50 g/L xylose (pH 5.6).
Incubate the 50% SGH challenge cultures in the deep well plate system for 72 hours to obtain A620 at ~10.
Inoculate a 16 ml aliquot of SGH-N1 or SGH-N2 with the cell pellet (15 min, 2,711 x g) from three wells of challenge culture to yield initial test culture A620 ~2.0.
Incubate test cultures at 25 °C, 180 rpm (1" orbit) in 25 ml flasks with silicone sponge closures.
Sample flasks daily and analyze per the PSGHL screen.
Screen isolates using steps 12.2 and 12.3, but substitute SGH-N1 and SGH-N2 with 6% glucan AFEX CSH at pH 5.2 for preparing the challenge culture medium and test culture medium.
For 50% strength challenge cultures, use 6% AFEX CSH diluted 1:1 with water since it is nitrogen sufficient without amendment.
Repeat steps 12.1-12.4 to duplicate results.
Rank performances of isolates in the secondary screen using RPI overall to rate use of multiple complete hydrolyzates.

Score each isolate tested in the secondary screen based on xylose uptake rate and ethanol yield performed on three enzyme-saccharified pretreated hydrolyzate formulations run in duplicate, including AFEX CSH (i = 1 and 2), SGH-N1 (i = 3 and 4) and SGH-N2 (i = 5 and 6).
Calculate the RPIoverall for each isolate.
Apply this ranking parameter to further winnow the list of superior isolates: RPIoverall = Σi=1,n[(RPIY +RPIR)/2]i/n, where n = 6.
